## Why A typical PR takes about 13 minutes because smoke, Playwright, Maestro, and the GCP preview each run their slow steps one after another. ## What changed - Smoke compiles in one job and exports admin-spa, demo, and example-frontend in three others, then runs the package smokes. - Playwright prepare compiles and exports together. The long `app` shard is now `app-todos`, `app-shell`, and `app-ai`. - Maestro installs Java and compiles while the web export runs. - A GCP preview builds the example-backend image once and deploys the backend and tasks services together. - `api-ci` runs two shards. Each starts its own memory Mongo. ## Verification | Status | Scope | Evidence / action | | --- | --- | --- | | ✅ Tested | Shard wiring, source resolver, parallel runner | `bun test` on the CI scripts: 26 pass | | ⚠️ Not tested | Real CircleCI duration | This PR's pipeline is the measurement. If branch protection still requires `e2e-app`, replace it with `e2e-app-todos`, `e2e-app-shell`, and `e2e-app-ai`. |
  
--- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Touches production Docker image build and GCP preview deploy orchestration; incorrect parallelism could break CI or previews, but application runtime/auth logic is largely unchanged. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit ef8588996291ff81a03d1847d18c5dfa5881376a. ### Architectural review

**Assessment:** No comment | 3 prior finding comment(s) preserved

**Scope:** Incremental review of changes since `faacbd8`.

The incremental changes raise no new architectural concerns. `app-shell` now lists `${APP}/settings/**` again, which closes the earlier gap where non-mcp settings routes reached no app shard through the affected gate. The `smoke-compile` archive now keeps `admin-spa/src/dist` (the compiled `AdminSpaServeApp` plugin) and leaves out only the `admin-spa/dist` web export. A config test and a `test -f` check in the smoke job guard that, and the CircleCI how-to page explains it. In `metroFromSource.js`, `replaceAll` makes export patterns that contain more than one `*` resolve correctly.

<details>
<summary>Prior review summary</summary>

The CI parallelization is well structured: it adds shared helpers and keeps docs and tests in step. The main risks are that the production admin-spa image and every smoke or e2e web bundle now resolve `@terreno/*` from source, so dist packaging goes untested. Production build config also now depends on `scripts/ci/`, and the app-shard split dropped affected-gate coverage for non-mcp settings routes.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Suggested refactors (2)</summary>

- Move `metroFromSource.js` out of `scripts/ci/` into a shared Metro config helper, since three app configs and the production Dockerfile now depend on it.
- Move the Docker compile and export script into a build-scripts location so the production image does not depend on the CI directory layout.

</details>

No new material architectural concerns identified in the latest changes.
